n: A twin to Psalm 111 and also an acrostic. Psalm 111 praised God’s character; Psalm 112 shows that character reflected in the person who reverences him and delights in his commandments.
The children of such a person will be strong and influential; the upright family line is blessed.
Prosperity fills his house, and his righteousness lasts forever — the very phrase used of God in Psalm 111:3.
Light dawns for the upright even in dark times. He is gracious, compassionate, and just — the same qualities as God (111:4).
A good person is generous and lends freely, and conducts business with justice.
He will never be shaken, and the righteous will be remembered forever.
Bad news doesn’t terrify him, because his heart is firmly anchored in trust in the Lord.
His heart is secure and unafraid; he will see his enemies’ threats come to nothing.
He gives generously to the poor. Paul quotes this verse to encourage cheerful giving. His ‘horn’ (dignity) will be lifted in honor.

f.w: he hath given to the poor

n: The wicked see it and are angry, grinding their teeth in frustration, but their desires will come to nothing — a contrast that echoes Psalm 1.

f.w: the desire of the wicked shall perish
